name: Fractured World 2045
description: The mid-century: climate shocks, machine minds, orbital assets, and a multipolar order held together with tape. The old hegemony is gone — what replaces it is being decided now.

USA.name: American Federation
USA.note: Reconstituted after the turbulent thirties, fusion-powered and inward-looking — a superpower unsure it still wants the job.

CHN.name: China
CHN.note: The first automation superpower, rich, gray, and shrinking — projecting power abroad to quiet the demographics at home.

IND.name: India
IND.note: The world's largest economy by heads and rising by every other measure, monsoon-whipsawed and ferociously self-confident.

DEU.name: European Federation
DEU.note: The Berlin-Paris core of a federated Europe: rich, regulated, and heavily fortified against the migration century. (Mapped on the German core; the union extends beyond.)

RUS.name: Russia
RUS.note: Diminished and thawing — literally: the Arctic coast is the last great prize, and Moscow guards it jealously.

BRA.name: Brazil
BRA.note: Steward of the Amazon Compact and breadbasket to three continents; biotech and carbon credits made it a great power at last.

NGA.name: Nigeria
NGA.note: Africa's demographic colossus — 400 million people, a booming solar belt, and Lagos as the hemisphere's loudest cultural capital.

IDN.name: Indonesia
IDN.note: Astride the world's most vital straits with the drones to close them, drowning and building seawalls at the same time.

world.simulationRules: Mid-century logic: climate disruption is a permanent actor — storms, crop failures, water disputes, and migration waves stress every government. AI and automation reshape labor, warfare, and intelligence; attribution is hard and deniable operations are the norm. Orbital and cyber domains are contested infrastructure. Chip, rare-earth, and food supply chains are leverage. Nuclear deterrence still holds, so great powers collide through proxies, standards, sanctions, and swarms — but a hot war over the Arctic, the straits, or orbit is no longer unthinkable.
